title: Cross-SDK failure ontology + guided repair steps (Python / TS / Go)
creator: Connor Lee
description:
Problem:
Teams building on Redwood consistently surface different error shapes across Python/TS/Go SDKs. Customers see opaque messages for transient failures, unclear retry guidance for streaming interruptions, and language idioms are inconsistent (exceptions vs error values). This increases support load and causes incorrect retry logic in customer code.

Objective:
Define and implement a cross-SDK failure ontology and developer-facing repair guidance so that: error classification (transient vs terminal vs throttling) is consistent across languages; ergonomic language-native surfaces provide actionable fields (retry_after, idempotency_hint, resume_token); and customers receive concise, prescriptive remediation steps.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Schema: a single canonical failure ontology (string error_code, human_message, category, retryable, retry_after_seconds, resume_token_hint, idempotency_key_hint, diagnostic_id).
- Language bindings: Python (Exception subclasses + attributes), TypeScript (Error subclasses / typed error discriminants), Go (wrapped error types with sentinel codes and Unwrap/Is helpers).
- Streaming ergonomics: standard resume_token format, clear guidance for when to resume vs restart stream, and helper utilities in each SDK to resume safely.
- Retry guidance: embed actionable retry hints (fixed backoff / exponential suggestion), and map service-level retryable flags to SDK retry policies.
- Telemetry: attach failure_hint and diagnostic_id to logs and Console traces for fast debugging.
- Migration plan: backward-compatible fallbacks; opt-in feature gate for strict typing.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDKs surface the canonical 'error_code' and 'retryable' field in a language-idiomatic way in emitted errors.
2) Streaming interruptions include 'resume_token_hint' when safe to resume, and SDK helpers can demonstrate resume in an example.
3) End-to-end unit + integration tests for Python/TS/Go cover transient, terminal, throttling, and streaming resume cases.
4) Documentation page and a short migration guide (examples for converting from previous SDKs) published to Confluence and the public docs site.
5) One end-to-end customer incident recreated in staging to validate signal propagation to Console (trace links + diagnostic_id).

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Single canonical schema avoids divergent interpretations but requires language-specific ergonomics. We will keep the shape minimal (the listed fields) to limit breaking changes.
- Go will use error.Is()/errors.As() with sentinel codes to preserve idiomatic error handling; this sacrifices having attributes directly on the error value but makes pattern matching simple.
- Python will prefer Exception subclasses with properties for quick access (e.g., e.error_code).
- TypeScript will use a tagged union on Error with 'code' and a typed helper isRetryable(err).
- For streaming resume, we choose deterministic resume_token_hint (opaque base64 string) from the service. We will not attempt full client-side seq reconciliation in v1 to limit risk.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Draft canonical failure ontology and examples (this ticket). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Failure+Ontology+Proposal
2) Prototype python errors and ts error tagging; internal review cycle. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2897
3) Implement Go sentinel codes + helpers; small adapter to surface resume tokens. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/402
4) Add integration tests in the infra/staging harness (simulate transient 503s, throttling 429s, streaming cut mid-sequence). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/runtimes/errors-telemetry (internal)
5) Docs + migration / snippet examples; ship v1 opt-in flag and announce in release notes.

Migration & rollout:
- Feature gate: "structured-errors-v1" to be enabled per client by default for new minor releases, opt-out by env var for compatibility.
- Automate a smoke test against staging for 24h before flipping default.
- Coordinate with support & Solutions Eng on canned remediation steps and playbooks.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Customers parsing freeform messages will break. Mitigation: keep human_message and error_code stable; add migration instructions and a mapping table.
- Risk: Language bindings diverge in implementation quality. Mitigation: cross-language design review and shared unit test harness (common test vectors repository).
- Risk: resume token semantics ambiguous. Mitigation: service will include 'resume_safety' flag with values safe/unsafe and SDKs will refuse to resume on unsafe.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay particular attention to the Go sentinel approach (trade-off of ergonomics vs idiomatic patterns).
- Security: error payload must not leak PII or secrets — see security checklist in Confluence.

Related artifacts:
- Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Failure+Ontology+Proposal
- Example migration guide (in progress): https://docs.redwood.ai/errors/migration-v1
- Prototype PR (Python/TS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2897
- Go PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/402
- Test vectors repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/error-test-vectors
